_comment: Environment + provider defaults used by authoring agents and page templates.
_templateComment: Notes-page template the authors copy (D-0031): the promoted W1D2 page. args_for.py passes it as args.template; when the file is missing it falls back to harness/templates/day.exemplar.html, which stays the structure gold standard for the tests.

audience._comment: Learner persona (D-0023, superseded by D-0048). Reaches every author/critic prompt as 'Audience'. Change via a decision entry.
audience.summary: Recent computer-science graduates (University of Toronto cohort) with no industry experience. Backgrounds vary and what each trainee retained is unknown.
assumeKnown: general programming ideas from any language: a variable, a branch, a loop, a function
assumeNotKnown: Python: its syntax, types, idioms and standard library
Git and GitHub, including clone, add, commit and push
the terminal: shells, paths, running a program from a prompt
CS theory: compilers vs interpreters, data structures, OOP
audience.rule: Never write that the reader already knows something, met it in coursework or remembers it. Teach each idea on its home day; an idea used before its home day gets a one-line explanation where it is used.
emphasise: how professional teams actually work: SDLC, Scrum, code review, written communication
Python from first principles: the syntax first, then the idioms, conventions and pitfalls a team expects
Git from first principles, then the team workflow: branches, merges, conflicts, remotes, commit hygiene
theory taught briefly and concretely, then practice

learnerRepo._comment: Learner repo convention (D-0051, supersedes D-0037): one PUBLIC repository per trainee inside the cohort organisation, created in the W1D2 Git exercise and kept for the whole course. Reaches every exercise and runbook author/critic prompt through args_for.py and day-fanout.js (learnerCtx). The trainer's live demo repository is demoRepo below, a different repository. Change via a decision entry.
learnerRepo.name: FirstnameLastname
learnerRepo.nameRule: the trainee's first and last name as on the class roster, run together in PascalCase, ASCII letters and digits; a hyphen or underscore between the names is tolerated; a clash gets a trailing digit

layout.root: hello.py, .gitignore and README.md from the W1D2 Git exercise stay at the top level
layout.exercises: <week-dir>/<day-slug>/, the same relative path the exercise has under exercises/ in the training repo
layout.hackathon: <week-dir>/hackathon/ for the week's hackathon deliverable, due on the week's last teaching day unless the trainer says otherwise
layout.codeAlong: optional: code-along/<week-dir>/<day-slug>/ for the trainee's own copy of what was typed in class; never marked

learnerRepo.handIn: commit and push to main; the trainer reads the day's folder in the trainee's repository

demoRepo._comment: The trainer's live demo repository (D-0050, D-0055): a PUBLIC GitHub repo separate from this one, cloned at localDir (gitignored, like trainer/). The trainer types live on branch (and the week plan's feature branches); harness/workflows/demo-series.js authors each week's blocks as one commit per block on prepBranch (WW = zero-padded week number), which is the answer key of every walkthrough; harness/close_day.py diffs the day's live commits against those prep commits to close a day. Thread code lives under threads.<id>.repoDir. Change via a decision entry.
demoRepo.name: demos

layout.thread: <threads.<id>.repoDir>/ at the top level, e.g. ticket-desk/ticket_desk.py, one commit per block on the prep branch; the trainer's live commits on main follow the same ladder

llm.rule: Model ids are resolved in the research brief from current docs, never from memory.

models._comment: Per-stage model and effort for harness/workflows/day-fanout.js, demo-series.js, week-plan.js and practice-tasks.js (D-0026, D-0032, D-0040, D-0047, D-0055). model: sonnet | haiku | opus; effort: low | medium | high | xhigh | max. Every stage is pinned: no stage inherits the session model (D-0040), and tests/test_notes_mode.py fails a null. A repass numbered >= escalateOn uses escalate instead of the stage tier, so a cheap first pass that fails its critic is retried on the strong tier. notes-critic judges the notes page; notes-verify-light runs harness/notes_check.py (links, stamps, citations) on every day; notes-verify-full adds WebFetch claim currency on full-gate and currency-flagged days. practice-suitability proposes practice tasks for an authored page and practice builds the approved ones (D-0047); their critic, verify and record agents use critic, verify and wire. demos authors one walkthrough block and demos-critic judges it against harness/critics/demos.md (D-0055); series-review is the one critic that reads a demo-series run's walkthroughs as a series at the end, flags only (D-0053). demos and runbook start on opus/high (D-0056): in the week-2 runs the sonnet first pass failed its critic on most items and the escalate tier ran anyway.

threads._comment: Demo threads (D-0033, D-0034, D-0050, D-0055): one demo codebase per project block that grows block by block across days and weeks (a block = one walkthrough = one commit on the week's prep branch). repoDir and file name where the thread lives inside demoRepo. args_for.py --plan passes the threads whose week range covers the week; the week-plan author may not invent a thread. Add P1/P2 threads via a decision entry before their first week is planned.

p0-ticket-desk.domain: A support-ticket desk for a small software team: tickets with a title, priority, status and history, filed by customers and triaged by agents. Week 1 keeps tickets in Python variables, lists, dicts and classes; week 2 splits the desk into modules with logging, keeps tickets in JSON files with error handling, puts resolution hours in NumPy arrays tested with pytest, loads the tickets into a pandas DataFrame and draws a Matplotlib chart of tickets per status; week 3 moves tickets, customers and agents into MySQL 9.7 tables in a Docker container (D-0059), with joins and transactions on assignment, reached from Python through mysql-connector-python; week 4 loads ticket events into a BigQuery star schema through an ETL job; week 5 sends tickets to an LLM for triage, summaries and draft replies.

tracker._comment: Alarm thresholds for tracker.html (D-0035), in calendar days. Readiness follows the previous-Friday rule: a day that is still planned (neither authored nor live, D-0052) turns amber dayAmberDaysBeforeWeek days before its week's Monday (the Wednesday before) and red dayRedDaysBeforeWeek days before (the Friday before); an authored day that is not live turns red from its week's Monday (authored, not released). The browser applies these to today's date; harness/build_tracker.py only embeds them.
